data.long_meaning: The name Akhalesh is derived from Sanskrit words 'Akha' meaning 'Immortal' and 'Ish' meaning 'Lord'. This name represents the divine and immortal being who governs the universe. The name Akhalesh carries the meaning “Immortal Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Akhalesh usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of eternal existence and divine power.
data.etymology: Akhalesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akhalesh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Akhalesh holds significant cultural impact in Hinduism. In Hindu mythology, the name 'Akh' is linked to the concept of immortality and is associated with the deity Yama, the God of Death, who grants immortality to the souls of those who attain Moksha, liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Thus, the name Akhalesh embodies the essence of transcendence and divine manifestation in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: For the spiritually inclined, the name Akhalesh carries immense significance. It represents the idea of a divine and supreme power that is eternal, unchanging, and beyond the cycles of birth and death. The name Akhalesh, as a reminder of the ultimate reality, can serve as an inspiration to live a life dedicated to the higher truth, love, and devotion. Ultimately, it is a name that evokes a sense of reverence, wonder, and awe towards the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Akhalesh signifies the one who is beyond the temporal world, untouched by the cycle of birth and death. The eternal soul, unchanging and timeless.

historical_references.reference: Akhalesh was a celebrated sage and a disciple of the great sage Vedavyasa. He was the author of the Mahabharata Anushasana Parva.
historical_references.context: Anushasana Parva is a part of the Mahabharata, a major Sanskrit epic of ancient India, which is attributed to Vyasa. It is one of the two major Sanskrit epic poems of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana.

historical_references.reference: Akhilesh is mentioned in various Hindu texts as a king of ancient India, particularly in the Puranas, where he is described as a great warrior and a devotee of Lord Vishnu. He is said to have ruled the kingdom of Haihayas in the region of Mathura.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a genre of ancient Indian literature, primarily in Sanskrit, dealing with various aspects of Hinduism. They are considered as one of the important sources of ancient Indian history, mythology, philosophy, and socio-cultural traditions.
